# Breeze — Full Reference

> Shenzhen engineering partner for AI hardware. Concept → production. Real numbers. Open data.

## What Breeze Does

Breeze is a Shenzhen engineering services firm. We do not sell hardware. We sell engineering and project management for a monthly fee. Third-party costs are passed through at cost. Our typical engagement covers BOM cost optimization, design-for-manufacturing review, prototype runs, factory selection, and certification navigation (FCC, CE, UKCA, RCM, CCC).

We work with founders building AI-enabled wearables, sensors, edge devices, and consumer hardware. Our minimum production volume is 1K — far below typical contract manufacturers' 10K+ MOQ.

## Why we publish open tools

Most engineering services firms hide their numbers. We publish our 1K-volume BOM pricing, our NRE estimates, our DFM checklists, and our certification matrices as open-source data on GitHub (MIT licensed). The four tools at /tools/* are powered by the same data, served as interactive calculators. Founders can audit our numbers before they ever talk to us. If our pricing is wrong, the GitHub repo will show it.

## Tools — detailed

### BOM Cost Estimator (/tools/bom-estimator)

Computes 1K-volume bill-of-materials cost for AI-hardware designs. Coverage:
- **MCUs / SoCs**: ESP32-S3 (Espressif), RV1103, RK3562, RK3588S (Rockchip), Genio 350/700 (MediaTek)
- **Sensors**: IMU, microphone arrays, ToF, camera modules
- **Power**: PMIC, battery management, USB-C PD
- **Memory**: SPI flash, eMMC, LPDDR4
- **Wireless**: BLE, Wi-Fi 6, LoRa, cellular modules

Outputs low/mid/high BOM tiers plus volume scaling. Email submission triggers a PDF report.

### NRE Simulator (/tools/nre-simulator)

Estimates non-recurring engineering cost for a first production run. Categories:
- Industrial design + mechanical engineering
- PCB schematic + layout (rev cycles)
- Firmware development
- Tooling (injection molds, jigs, fixtures)
- Certifications (FCC, CE, etc. — standards selectable)
- Engineering prototypes
- Pilot production setup

Outputs a phased timeline with month-by-month cost. Email submission triggers a PDF report.

### DFM Checklist (/tools/dfm-checklist)

Design-for-manufacturing review across categories:
- Thermal management
- RF / antenna integration
- PCB layout (DFA, panelization, test points)
- Mechanical (tolerance stacks, snap-fits, draft angles)
- Certification readiness (radio, EMC, safety)
- Supply chain risk (single-source components, lifecycle)

Each item rated pass / fail / not-applicable. Surfaces the common first-product failures founders hit late.

### Cert Navigator (/tools/cert-navigator)

Selects required certifications by target market and device features:
- **Markets**: US (FCC), EU (CE/RED/EMC/RoHS), UK (UKCA), AU (RCM), CN (CCC + SRRC + CMIIT)
- **Features**: BLE, Wi-Fi, cellular, battery type, mains-powered, pacemaker-adjacent, child-targeted

Outputs typical cost range, lead time, and which lab to use.

## Guides

- [How much does it cost to build an AI hardware device? (2026)](https://breezehw.com/ai-hardware-cost): per-unit cost at 1,000 units for three example builds (voice pendant, camera device, screen + local AI), what volume does to price, one-time engineering, tooling and certification ranges, and why memory is now the line to watch. Computed from the same data as the BOM and NRE tools.
- [EVT, DVT and PVT for AI hardware: what each stage must prove](https://breezehw.com/evt-dvt-pvt): units and weeks per stage, the checks that matter most for AI devices (on-device model accuracy, sustained-inference thermals, OTA recovery, production yield), and the stop conditions for each stage. Checked against the open toolkit checklist.
- [What to check before an AI-made hardware design goes to a factory](https://breezehw.com/ai-design-to-factory): where AI CAD, schematic, layout and firmware tools work and where they break (November 2026, each number sourced), four published failures, a three-layer checklist, and the handoff package a factory asks for.

## Open data

[AI Hardware Toolkit](https://github.com/jianjettfu-oss/ai-hardware-toolkit) — the open-source data and checklists behind every Breeze tool. License: MIT. The toolkit includes BOM pricing CSVs, NRE templates, DFM checklists in Markdown, certification matrices (including EU cybersecurity, Cyber Resilience Act and battery rules), and an AI-made-design handoff checklist. For AI agents it ships six Agent Skills as a Claude Code plugin (`/plugin marketplace add jianjettfu-oss/ai-hardware-toolkit`), Cursor rules, an MCP server and a Custom GPT knowledge file, all generated from the same topic files. Contributions welcome.

## Typical product cost (not our fee)

For most AI wearables and connected devices, total NRE (engineering, tooling, samples, certification) runs $50K-$150K. Per-unit cost depends mostly on the chip and the memory: at 5K units our November 2026 estimates run from about $20 for an MCU-class voice pendant to about $61 for a camera device on a Linux SoC and $110 with a screen and a local model (parts behind each figure: https://breezehw.com/ai-hardware-cost). Complexity (sensors, radios, battery chemistry, certifications) drives the range. The NRE Simulator gives a tailored ballpark: https://breezehw.com/tools/nre-simulator

## Engagement model

- **Feasibility and sourcing sprint** — $3-5K, fixed, 2-3 weeks.
- **Prototype to pilot** — $4-8K per month, usually 3-6 months.
- **Production management** — $3-6K per month per product.
- **Third-party costs** — parts, tooling, samples, test labs, and specialist engineering are passed through at cost.
- **Fixed project total** — can be quoted after the sprint.
- **Cash only** — no equity.
- **NDA + IP assignment** — standard on every engagement. Designs stay yours.
- **Production from 1,000 units** — pilots of 50–500 units come first; under 100 units, case by case. Most factories ask for 10K+.
- **No equity ever** — we work for fees, not founder equity.

## How to engage

1. Run the tools at /tools/* to ballpark cost.
2. Email hello@breezehw.com with your concept (one paragraph).
3. We respond within 2 business days with a feasibility assessment.
4. If both sides see fit, we start with a feasibility and sourcing sprint. After it, we can quote a fixed total for the project.

## What Breeze does NOT do

- Take equity for engineering work.
- Build with 10K+ MOQ minimums.
- Hide BOM costs behind NDAs (our data is public).
- Recommend certification labs we have undisclosed kickback arrangements with.
- White-label other firms' work.
